newsitem.title: USA: Consumers sees Mich. power plant back Tues.
newsitem.headline: Consumers sees Mich. power plant back Tues.

text.p: Consumers Energy said Tuesday it has shut its 780 megawatt (MW) Palisades nuclear power plant for repairs, and that the unit likely will be back on line late Tuesday and at full power within a couple of days.
"We could be on line later tonight. Full power will take a day or two," company spokesman Mark Savage said.
The unit, in South Haven, Mich., was at about half power late last week to correct a vibration on the isophase bus.
The decision to fully shut the unit followed the discovery Monday at about 0200 CST of a hydrogen leak on the unit's main generator, he said. Hydrogen is used as a cooling agent within the generator.
Consumers Energy is a subsidiary of CMS Energy Corp.
